slope/line: A straight line climbs at the same rate everywhere. Two x plus one rises two for every step of one, so its slope is two.
slope/curve: A curve is steeper in some places than others. Take f of x equals x squared. How steep is it at x equals one?
slope/two: Pick a second point a step h to the right, at x equals two. Between them, f goes from one to four.
slope/rise: Rise over run is three over one. The slope between the two points is three.
shrink/shrink: Now shrink the step. With h equal to a half, the slope is two point five. With a tenth, it is two point one.
shrink/limit: As h shrinks toward zero, the slope settles on two. That limit is the derivative: f prime of one equals two.
shrink/tangent: The line with that slope just grazes the curve at x equals one. It is the tangent.
shrink/nudge: Read it as a rate. Nudge x by zero point zero one, and f moves by about twice as much: zero point zero two.
sign/slide: The derivative changes from point to point. Slide the tangent along the curve.
sign/neg: On the left, f falls as x grows, and the slope is negative: minus three, at minus one point five.
sign/zero: At the bottom the tangent is level, and the slope is zero.
sign/pos: On the right, f rises, and the slope is positive: three.
example/ask: Your turn to follow along. f of three is nine, and f of three and a half is twelve point two five. With h equal to a half, what is the slope between them?
example/rise: The rise is twelve point two five minus nine: three point two five.
example/run: Divide by the run, a half: three point two five over a half is six point five.
example/close: That is close to the slope right at three, which is six. A smaller step would land closer still.
